entries.name: Frontmatter
entries.summary: The frontmatter keys this reader uses. Other keys are ignored, so a page may carry metadata for something else.

entries.name: ListItem
entries.summary: One item of a list: its own inline text, plus any blocks nested under it.

entries.name: MdBlock
entries.summary: A block of a Markdown document.

entries.name: Document
entries.summary: A parsed document: its frontmatter and its blocks.

entries.name: parseDocument
entries.summary: Parses a Markdown document. Windows line endings are accepted.

entries.name: toHtml
entries.summary: Returns the HTML for a document's body, ignoring its frontmatter.

entries.name: splitFrontmatter
entries.summary:
--- frontmatter -------------------------------------------------------

A leading `---` fence delimits frontmatter. Without one the document is all body, and every field takes its default.

entries.name: assign
signatures: assign(front: Frontmatter, key: String, value: String) -> Frontmatter

entries.name: trimEnds
entries.summary: Drops the first and last character, the quotes `quoted?` matched.

entries.name: blockLoop
entries.summary: One pass over the lines, each branch consuming the whole construct it recognises and returning the lines it did not take.

entries.name: rule?
entries.summary: Returns `true` for a horizontal rule: three or more of `-`, `*` or `_` and nothing else on the line. Frontmatter is removed before this runs.

entries.name: headingLevel
entries.summary: Returns a heading's level, so `##` gives 2, or 0 when the line is not a heading. `#hashtag` is not one.

entries.name: takeCode
entries.summary:
--- fenced code -------------------------------------------------------

Takes a fenced code block. The word after the fence is the language. A fence that is never closed runs to the end of the document.

entries.name: takeQuote
entries.summary:
--- blockquotes -------------------------------------------------------

Takes a blockquote. The `>` is stripped from each line and the rest is parsed as blocks, so a quote can hold anything a document can.

entries.name: takeList
entries.summary:
--- lists -------------------------------------------------------------

Takes a list. A line indented past the first item's marker belongs to the item above it and is parsed as blocks, so an item can hold paragraphs, code and nested lists.

entries.name: listLine?
entries.summary: Returns `true` for a line that can continue a list: an item, an indented line or a blank line. The first other line ends the list.

entries.name: flushItem
entries.summary: Adds the collected item to `accum`. The first line is the item's text; the lines below it are dedented and parsed as nested blocks.

entries.name: dedent
entries.summary: Removes the common indent, so nested content is parsed at column zero.

entries.name: numberMarker
entries.summary: Returns a numbered-list marker, so `"12. "` gives `"12."`, or `""` when the line has none.

entries.name: tableStart?
entries.summary:
--- tables ------------------------------------------------------------

Returns `true` when the lines start a GFM table: a header row followed by a row of dashes. Without that row the lines are a paragraph.

entries.name: cellsOf
entries.summary: Returns the cells of a table row. Leading and trailing pipes are optional.

entries.name: takeParagraph
entries.summary:
--- paragraphs --------------------------------------------------------

Takes a paragraph, which ends at a blank line or where another block starts, so a list or code fence right under prose is not swallowed.

entries.name: renderCode
entries.summary: Renders a code block. Kex code goes through the reference pages' highlighter; other languages are escaped and left plain.

entries.name: anchor
entries.summary: Returns a heading's id: lower case, with each run of characters other than letters and digits turned into one dash.

entries.name: trimDashes
entries.summary: Removes dashes from both ends, which `anchor` can leave: `(try)` becomes `-try-` before this.

entries.name: stripInline
entries.summary: Returns the text with the inline markers (backticks, `*` and `_`) removed.

entries.name: inline
entries.summary:
--- inline ------------------------------------------------------------

Renders inline Markdown. Code spans are handled first: their content is escaped but not scanned for emphasis, so `a*b*c` in backticks stays as written.

entries.name: emphasis
entries.summary: Renders links, then bold and italics, so a `*` inside a URL is not read as a marker.

entries.name: linkParts
entries.summary: Splits `label](href)` and what follows it into `(label, href, rest)`, or returns `None` when it is not a link, and the `[` is plain text.

entries.name: marks
entries.summary: Renders bold before italics, or the opening `**` would be read as empty italics. The remaining text is escaped here.

entries.name: wrap
signatures: wrap(text: String, strongMark: String, strongTag: String, emMark: String, emTag: String) -> String

entries.name: pairs
signatures: pairs(text: String, mark: String, tag: String, accum: String) -> String
entries.summary: Replaces each pair of markers with a tag. A marker without a partner is left as written.

entries.name: indexOfText
signatures: indexOfText(haystack: String, needle: String, at: Integer) -> Integer?
entries.summary: Returns where `needle` first occurs in `haystack` from `at` on, or `None`. `String.indexOf` only finds a `Char`, and `**` is two characters.

entries.name: Extension
entries.summary:
One `make` block as seen from the type it extends: where it is, the names it adds and the traits it declares.

A type's functions can be spread over many files (there is a `make Integer` in number.kex, period.kex, units.kex and others), and these rows gather them on the type's page.

entries.name: TypeFacts
entries.summary:
Everything the package says about one type, across files.

`homePath` is the type's main page: the one declaring it, or for a builtin such as Integer or String the one named after it.

entries.name: TraitFacts
entries.summary: A trait seen from the outside: where it is documented and which make blocks implement it.

entries.name: ModuleIndexEntry
entries.summary:
One module of the package and the page its entities are on.

The sidebar and the module index of model.json are built from these. Readers navigate by module, and a module need not match a file.

entries.name: MemberEntry
entries.summary: One documented member of a module and the anchor of its section, for the sidebar and the JSON index.

entries.name: LinkEntry
entries.summary: One row of the cross-link index: a name that a type reference may mention, such as "String" or "FS.Path", and where it links to. Every renderer resolves names against this one list.

entries.name: PackageModel
entries.summary: Everything extracted from one package: its pages, modules, links and cross-file relations.

entries.name: SearchEntry
entries.summary:
One row of the search index, for an entity or for a function inside a trait, make or module.

`types` are the type names its signature mentions, so a search can match by type as well as by name. `anchor` is the section a result links to.

entries.name: VersionEntry
entries.summary: One row of versions.json. Each build adds or replaces its own `(package, id)` row in the file already in the output directory, so the file lists every version built there.

entries.name: kindOf
entries.summary: Returns the kind label an entity has in indexes and JSON, such as `"record"` or `"make"`.

entries.name: nameOf
entries.summary: Returns an entity's display name; a make's is its target type.

entries.name: anchorOf
entries.summary:
Returns the id of an entity's HTML section.

It is here, not in the HTML renderer, because the cross-link index and the sidebar need the same ids.

entries.name: anchorNameOf
entries.summary: Returns the text an entity's anchor is made from: a make's full target, type parameters included, or otherwise the qualified name.

entries.name: memberAnchorOf
entries.summary: Returns the anchor of a function documented inside a trait or make section. It includes the owner, because one page can hold several owners with a `count`, such as `[X]` and `String`.

entries.name: ownerSlugOf
entries.summary: Returns the slug of an owner type: `[X]` gives "list", `[Number]` gives "list-number" and `FileHandle<CanRead, W>` gives "filehandle-canread". Type variables (a capital letter, optionally followed by a digit) are dropped.

entries.name: wordsOf
entries.summary: Returns the runs of letters, digits, `_`, `?` and `!` in a type's text.

entries.name: slugOf
entries.summary: Returns a name spelled for an HTML id: lower case, with each run of punctuation turned into one dash. `?` and `!` are kept, as in `empty?`.

entries.name: operatorSlug
entries.summary: Returns the slug of an operator, which has no letters of its own: `<=>` gives "op-lt-eq-gt" and a plus sign "op-plus".

entries.name: baseTypeOf
entries.summary: Returns the type a make block extends, without its type arguments: "[X]" gives "List", "{K: V}" and "Map<K, V>" give "Map", and "FileHandle<R, W>" gives "FileHandle".

entries.name: Tey.Docgen.Nav
signatures: claimedByAnother?(pages: [SourcePage], page: SourcePage, title: String) -> Bool
memberLinks(ownerName: String, owner: String, functions: [Tey.Docgen.Model.FunctionEntry], urlPath: String) -> [LinkEntry]
splitLoop(rest: String, ident: String, sep: String, out: [String]) -> [String]
hrefFrom(fromPath: String, toPath: String, anchor: String) -> String

entries.name: buildModules
entries.summary: Returns an entry for every module in the package, in declaration order, with the page it is on. Nested modules get entries of their own.

entries.name: parentTitleOf
entries.summary:
Returns the title of the page that `page` nests under, or `None` for a top-level page.

The parent is found from titles, not paths: "Net.DNS" nests under "Net", and "Net.HTTP.WebSocket" under "Net.HTTP". The longest prefix that has a page wins. When no prefix has a page ("Control" for "Control.Retry"), the page is top-level.

entries.name: claimedByAnother?
signatures: claimedByAnother?(pages: [SourcePage], page: SourcePage, title: String) -> Bool

entries.name: topLevelPages
entries.summary: Returns the pages with no parent, sorted by title, for the sidebar's top level.

entries.name: childPages
entries.summary: Returns the pages nested directly under `title`, sorted by title.

entries.name: descendantPages
entries.summary: Returns every page nested under `page` at any depth, sorted by title. A module page lists these as its submodules.

entries.name: buildLinks
entries.summary:
Returns the names that can be linked, each with its page and anchor.

A name links only while exactly one place answers to it. A qualified name ("FS.Path") is usually unique; a simple one ("Path") stops linking as soon as two different entities share it, and then only the qualified names link.

entries.name: withTypeHomes
entries.summary:
Returns `links` plus a link to the home page of each type that make blocks extend and that does not link yet.

A name such as `Integer` is claimed by a module and by several make blocks, so `buildLinks` drops it. In a signature it means the type, which has a home page (`Relations.homePathOf`), so this adds that link. A name that already links keeps its link.

entries.name: memberLinks
signatures: memberLinks(ownerName: String, owner: String, functions: [Tey.Docgen.Model.FunctionEntry], urlPath: String) -> [LinkEntry]
entries.summary: Returns links for the functions of a trait or make block under their owner's name, so prose that writes `List.map` links to that function.

entries.name: linkableNames
entries.summary: Returns the names an entity can be linked under: its qualified name and its simple name. Functions have none of their own. A make block links under its target's base name, so "Map<K, V>" links as "Map"; a list target such as "[X]" does not link.

entries.name: uniqueTarget?
entries.summary: Returns `true` when every entry with `candidate`'s name points at the same page and anchor.

entries.name: segmentsOf
entries.summary: Splits a type reference into identifiers and the separators between them, so a renderer can link the identifiers: "Map<String, FS.Path>" gives ["Map", "<", "String", ", ", "FS.Path", ">"].

entries.name: splitLoop
signatures: splitLoop(rest: String, ident: String, sep: String, out: [String]) -> [String]
entries.summary: `ident` is the identifier being read, `sep` the separator run since it; only one is non-empty at a time, and whichever it is goes out in order.

entries.name: hrefFrom
signatures: hrefFrom(fromPath: String, toPath: String, anchor: String) -> String
entries.summary: Returns the relative href from one page of the package to an anchor on another: "#anchor" on the same page, otherwise a path up to the version directory and down to the target.

entries.name: Tey.Docgen.Prose
signatures: writeProse(pages: [ProsePage], versionDir: String, out: String, model: PackageModel) -> ()
writeProseLoop(pages: [ProsePage], index: Integer, versionDir: String, model: PackageModel) -> ()
prevLink(pages: [ProsePage], index: Integer, up: String) -> String
nextLink(pages: [ProsePage], index: Integer, up: String) -> String

entries.name: ProsePage
entries.summary: One Markdown page, read and rendered: its place in the site, its sort order and description from the frontmatter, its HTML, and the Markdown without frontmatter that is served as its `.md` version.

entries.name: writeProse
signatures: writeProse(pages: [ProsePage], versionDir: String, out: String, model: PackageModel) -> ()
entries.summary: Writes each page as HTML and as Markdown side by side, as reference builds do, plus the index page and the shared assets.

entries.name: writeProseLoop
signatures: writeProseLoop(pages: [ProsePage], index: Integer, versionDir: String, model: PackageModel) -> ()

entries.name: proseIndexHtml
entries.summary: Renders the index page: the chapters in the author's order, each with its description. Reference builds use `versionIndexHtml`, a grid of modules, instead; the two are kept separate so book layout never reaches `tey docs build`.

entries.name: prevNextHtml
entries.summary: Renders a chapter's footer: links to the previous and next chapters. The first and last chapters get only one link.

entries.name: prevLink
signatures: prevLink(pages: [ProsePage], index: Integer, up: String) -> String

entries.name: nextLink
signatures: nextLink(pages: [ProsePage], index: Integer, up: String) -> String

entries.name: Tey.Docgen.Rdoc
signatures: plusPair?(head: String, inner: String, tail: String) -> Bool
classifyBlocks(blocks: [[String]], summary: String, params: [Param], returns: Return?, examples: [Example], deprecated: String?) -> Doc?
findClosingBracket(s: String, index: Integer, depth: Integer) -> Integer?

entries.name: parseDoc
entries.summary: Parses a doc comment's text, or returns `None` for empty text.

entries.name: parseOrEmpty
entries.summary: Parses a doc comment's text, giving an empty `Doc` for empty text.

entries.name: rewriteProseBlocks
entries.summary:
Rewrites plus-sign code markup in each prose block separately, leaving verbatim blocks and `@example` code alone. `@param` and `@return` descriptions are prose and are rewritten.

A pair never spans two blocks. Rewriting the whole comment at once would pair the plus sign of an addition in a code sample with the next markup in the prose.

entries.name: plusPair?
signatures: plusPair?(head: String, inner: String, tail: String) -> Bool
entries.summary: Returns `true` when a pair of plus signs around `inner` is markup. There must be no space just inside either sign, so an addition with spaces stays as written; no backtick inside, so spans never nest; and no letter or digit just outside, so an addition without spaces stays too.

entries.name: splitParagraphs
entries.summary: Splits lines into blocks. Prose runs until a blank line. Every line that starts with `@` opens a block of its own, so consecutive `@param` lines stay separate, and the indented lines after a directive (an example's code) belong to it.

entries.name: indentWidth
entries.summary: Returns the number of leading spaces in a line.

entries.name: verbatim?
entries.summary: Returns `true` for a verbatim block: one whose every non-blank line is indented by at least two spaces, as RDoc marks code or a hand-laid-out table. Such a block keeps its line breaks and is carried into the summary as a fenced code block.

entries.name: dedent
entries.summary: Removes the indentation shared by every non-blank line, so a block renders flush left.

entries.name: mergeVerbatim
entries.summary: Joins adjacent verbatim blocks back together with a blank line between them, since a blank line inside a code sample does not end it.

entries.name: classifyBlocks
signatures: classifyBlocks(blocks: [[String]], summary: String, params: [Param], returns: Return?, examples: [Example], deprecated: String?) -> Doc?

entries.name: parseParam
entries.summary: Reads a `@param name [Type] description` directive.

entries.name: parseReturn
entries.summary: Reads a `@return [Type] description` directive.

entries.name: parseBracketed
entries.summary: Splits text that opens with a bracketed group, such as `[Integer] the count`, into the group's content and the rest. Returns `None` when the text does not open with one.

entries.name: findClosingBracket
signatures: findClosingBracket(s: String, index: Integer, depth: Integer) -> Integer?

entries.name: Tey.Docgen.Relations
signatures: typedByTrait(f: FunctionEntry, m: MakeEntry, traits: [TraitEntry]) -> FunctionEntry
extensionOf(page: SourcePage, entity: Entity, entry: MakeEntry) -> Extension
homeAnchorOf(base: String, home: String, mine: [Extension], pages: [SourcePage]) -> String
namesTrait?(written: String, name: String, qualifiedName: String) -> Bool

entries.name: withTraitSignatures
entries.summary:
Returns `pages` with each untyped make member that implements a trait function given the trait's signature.

For `let identity = 0` under `make Integer, implement: Monoid`, that is the signature `Monoid` declares, with `This` read as `Integer`. It runs on the pages before anything renders them, so every output shows the same signature.

entries.name: typedByTrait
signatures: typedByTrait(f: FunctionEntry, m: MakeEntry, traits: [TraitEntry]) -> FunctionEntry

entries.name: extensionOf
signatures: extensionOf(page: SourcePage, entity: Entity, entry: MakeEntry) -> Extension

entries.name: homePathOf
entries.summary:
Returns the page a type's links should go to.

That is the page declaring the type; failing that, the page titled after it (string.kex for the built-in String); then a page with both the type's companion module and a make block for it; and last the page whose make block adds the most functions, so number.kex for Integer rather than algebra.kex, which only makes it a Monoid.

entries.name: homeAnchorOf
signatures: homeAnchorOf(base: String, home: String, mine: [Extension], pages: [SourcePage]) -> String

entries.name: namesTrait?
signatures: namesTrait?(written: String, name: String, qualifiedName: String) -> Bool
entries.summary: Returns whether `written`, as it appears in an `implement:` list, names the trait `name`. `implement: Enumerable` and `implement: Kex.Enumerable` both name the trait declared as `Enumerable` inside `module Kex`.

entries.name: typeFactsFor
entries.summary: Returns the facts for the type that make target `base` extends, or `None` when no make block extends it.

entries.name: traitEntryFor
entries.summary: Returns the declaration of a trait, for its list of functions.

entries.name: traitMethods
entries.summary:
Returns a trait's functions as an implementor sees them: the required ones and the provided ones.

A function is required when the trait gives it no body and no `make <Trait>` block in any file gives it a default. The provided ones are the rest, plus any functions such a block adds that the trait does not declare.

entries.name: traitTarget?
entries.summary: Returns whether a make target names a trait of this package.

entries.name: allFunctions
entries.summary: Returns every function documented in `entities`: top-level and module functions, trait functions and make members.

entries.name: required?
entries.summary: Returns whether a trait function has no body, so an implementor must write it.

entries.name: proseFiles
entries.summary: Returns the `.md` files under `sourceDir` that `tey docs prose` reads, found by the same walk as the `.kex` sources.

entries.name: routesFor
entries.summary: Returns the URL paths that serve a file. The router matches paths exactly, so an index.html gets three: its own path, its directory, and its directory with a trailing slash. Any other file gets only its own path.

entries.name: serveFile
entries.summary: Serves the file at `filePath`; `~serveFile(path)` is a route handler. The file is read as bytes, so images and fonts are served intact, and the response says `no-cache` because the site is rebuilt in place.
